next_question: Does SPA redesign with 0% deterministic strata (all transitions stochastic) eliminate the per-stratum plug-in PMI null bias on stochastic strata, where the bias persists at +0.742 bits even for strata of size 5-9 under the shuffled-action null — and does this redesign enable a valid beyond-Markov test, or is the bias intrinsic to plug-in estimation regardless of determinism ratio?
why_next: This experiment falsifies the estimator-level-bias-correction pathway: all four estimators (weighted, equal-weight, median, KNN) fail |null_mean|<0.1 by 2.6-7.0x margins. The mechanistic decomposition reveals the bias is monotonically increasing in small strata (+0.742 at size 5-9 vs +0.379 at size 20-49) and persists in stochastic strata — not just deterministic ones. The preregistered hypothesis H1 (bias from large-stratum dominance) is falsified: equal-weight/median worsen bias. The parent's open question about whether 0% deterministic strata would eliminate bias is now the critical fork: if bias persists in a fully stochastic SPA, the problem is intrinsic to plug-in estimation and truly orthogonal frameworks (KSG CMI, Bayesian, likelihood-ratio) are needed; if bias disappears, SPA redesign opens the PMI research program. This question directly tests the audit's V5 finding (bias persists in stochastic strata) and determines the future direction of the Physics lane.

established: Weighted-averaged PMI estimator is asymptotically non-convergent: K2 PMI grows from 0.933 (N=5000) to 1.779 (N=50000, +84.5%). (EXP-PHYSICS-35403136807 result.json; EXP-PHYSICS-35445596894 audit V6)

Per-stratum plug-in PMI null bias is monotonically decreasing in stratum size: +0.742 bits at size 5-9, +0.571 at 10-19, +0.379 at 20-49 (weighted framework, shuffled-action null, K2 records). Small strata carry the bias. (EXP-PHYSICS-35445596894 result.json:metrics.stratum_size_bias_decomposition, audit V5)

Equal-weight and median PMI corrections worsen aggregate null bias (0.704/0.686 vs 0.407 bits) by up-weighting the most biased small strata. The preregistered H1 hypothesis (bias from large-stratum dominance) is falsified. (EXP-PHYSICS-35445596894 result.json:controls.B-EQUAL-WEIGHT-PMI/B-MEDIAN-PMI)

KNN CMI (k=5, alpha=1.0) produces negative null bias (-0.262 bits) from Laplace smoothing + extra action dimension depressing P(Y|Z,X) below P(Y|Z). (EXP-PHYSICS-35445596894 result.json:controls.B-KNN-CMI, audit V7)

No estimator (weighted, equal-weight, median, KNN) converges at N=50000: all drift >0.2 bits (weighted +0.845, equal +0.247, median +0.373, KNN +1.261). Convergence is not achievable with these estimators on this SPA at these sample sizes. (EXP-PHYSICS-35445596894 result.json:metrics.n50000_descriptive_non_gating, audit V6)

Positive control validates all four estimator pipelines on 8-state deterministic SPA: K3 1.81-1.87 bits, p=0.000999. C1 failures are not execution defects. (EXP-PHYSICS-35445596894 result.json:controls.C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL, audit V3)

K2 PMI = 0.933 bits and K3 PMI = 1.221 bits are reproducible point estimates (weighted estimator replicates parent exactly). Reproducibility confirmed; interpretability remains the issue. (EXP-PHYSICS-35445596894 audit V1, provenance.json)

SPA environment has beyond-Markov structure by construction: choose_next(current,action,prev1,prev2) depends on 2-step history, so a valid estimator SHOULD detect K3>K2. (EXP-PHYSICS-35403136807 audit V9, EXP-PHYSICS-35445596894 run_experiment.py:CANDIDATES/choose_next)

Parent packet determinism_K3 record (467/821, det_ratio 0.569) is not reproducible from parent code+data; correct K3 det_ratio is 0.108 (89/821). K3 strata are more stochastic-fragmented than parent implied. (EXP-PHYSICS-35445596894 result.json:metrics.determinism_n5000, audit V4)

do_not_assume: C-WEB-DYNAMICS is globally false. The 0.933-bit K2 PMI signal is real and reproducible. FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING is bounded to estimator-bias-correction on this SPA class, not the claim itself.
Null bias is evidence against beyond-Markov signal. The permutation bias is intrinsic to plug-in stratum PMI estimation; it prevents interpretation but does not falsify the underlying dynamics.
All PMI null frameworks are exhausted. Truly orthogonal frameworks (KSG, Bayesian, likelihood-ratio) are untested.
The bias floor of ~0.41 bits at N=5000 is irreducible by SPA redesign. The stratum-size decomposition shows bias persists in stochastic strata, but a 0% deterministic SPA has not been tested.
K3-K2 difference of 0.287 bits (weighted) or 0.180 bits (KNN) reflects genuine beyond-Markov signal. All point estimates are uninterpretable without valid null centering.
SPA redesign to 0% deterministic strata is guaranteed to eliminate bias. The bias persists in stochastic strata (audit V5), so redesign may NOT work — this must be tested, not assumed.
Production SPA results generalize from this simulation. The 12-state SPA has 12 states, 4 deterministic candidates, hash-based selection, no anti-bot/auth/visual complexity.

recommended_action: Design an SPA-redesign experiment: construct a 12-state hash-routed SPA with 0% deterministic strata (all transitions stochastic via CANDIDATES[current][action][hash(...) % N] where N > 1 for every (current, action) pair). Run the same 4-estimator screening (weighted, equal-weight, median, KNN) at N=5000 with the same null control (shuffled-action, N_SHUFFLE=500, |mean| < 0.1). If null bias is eliminated (|mean| < 0.1 for any estimator), proceed to K3-K2 beyond-Markov testing. If bias persists, the problem is intrinsic to plug-in estimation and truly orthogonal frameworks (KSG CMI, Bayesian model comparison) are the required next attack. The stratum-size bias decomposition should be repeated on the redesigned SPA to confirm whether the +0.742 small-stratum bias disappears when deterministic strata are removed.
